[[File:Prisma heptagonal 3D.stl|thumb|3D model of a uniform heptagonal prism]]
In [[geometry]], the '''heptagonal prism''' is a [[Prism (geometry)|prism]] with [[heptagon]]al base. This [[polyhedron]] has 9 faces (2 bases and 7 sides), 21 edges, and 14 vertices.<ref name="pye">{{cite web
 |url=https://www.problemasyecuaciones.com/geometria3D/volumen/prisma/heptagonal/calculadora-area-volumen-formulas-demostracion.html
 |title=Area and volume calculator of a heptagonal prism |last=Sapiña |first=R. |publisher=Problemas y ecuaciones |issn=2659-9899 |language=es
 |access-date=June 17, 2020}}</ref><ref name="pugh">{{citation|title=Polyheda: A Visual Approach|first=Anthony|last=Pugh|publisher=University of California Press|year=1976|isbn=9780520030565|pages=27|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IDDxpYQTR7kC&pg=PA21}}.</ref>

== Area ==
The [[area]] of a right heptagonal prism with height <math>h</math> and with a side length of <math>L</math> and [[apothem]] <math>a_p</math> is given by:<ref name="pye" />
:<math>A = 7L\cdot (a_p + h)</math>

== Volume ==

The [[volume]] is found by taking the area of the base, with a side length of <math>L</math> and apothem <math>a_p</math>, and multiplying it by the height <math>h</math>, giving the formula:<ref name="pye" />
:<math>V = \frac{7}{2}\cdot h\cdot L\cdot a_p</math>

This formula also works for the oblique prism due to the  [[Cavalieri's principle]].
